recommendation: Keep this audit. Future primitive regex semantic changes should be handled under the specific later datatype tracker for the affected regex, not as missing FHIR-12959 application work.
issue_request: FHIR-12959 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-core datatypes issue asking that missing regular expressions for boolean, decimal, base64Binary, and instant be present either in source or on the datatypes documentation page.
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies svn revision 12461. In git, ffb483245175ff499a837bc605277a047ffa7b12 has the matching git-svn-id build@12461 and added primitive regex rows to source/datatypes.html plus RegEx-column values in source/datatypes/primitives.xml.
additional_context: The current datatypes page now uses [%regex ...%] macros rather than copied literal regex text, while source/datatypes/primitives.xml remains the primitive regex source. Later datatype issues refined these regexes, including FHIR-34099 for base64Binary and FHIR-22655/FHIR-53492 for decimal, without reversing the FHIR-12959 coverage decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing the original DSTU2 literal regexes would duplicate generated macro content and would risk undoing later approved corrections.

related_jiras.note: The same svn/git application commit handled the related primitive negative-example request, which already has a separate AutoFHIR audit on the combined branch.

Later corrected a decimal regex syntax issue after the original application.
